# Morgenruf

> An open source Slack bot for async standups, random coffee
> chats and peer recognition. It asks each team member the day's questions in
> a direct message, collects the answers, and posts one summary to a channel.
> MIT licensed and free with no per-seat pricing: on a hosted instance run by
> CloudDrove, or self-hosted. Built by Anmol Nagpal in Kitchener, Ontario,
> Canada, and sponsored by CloudDrove.

Morgenruf exists because the tools that do this charge per person for
something a team can run itself. Geekbot is free for up to 10 users, then $3
per user per month, or $2.50 per user per month billed annually. Donut has a
free plan (24 people per intro round) and paid plans from about $74 a month.
Those prices were checked 2026-09-26. HeyTaco is about $3 per user per month.
Morgenruf does all three jobs for nothing: free on a hosted instance run by
CloudDrove, or self-hosted, in which case the team keeps its own data on its
own servers.

## What it does

Standups
- Asks configurable questions by Slack direct message on a schedule
- Collects answers and posts a formatted summary to a channel
- Per-user timezones, so a distributed team is asked at a sensible local hour
- Highlights blockers, tracks participation streaks and team mood
- Skip a day, mark vacation, or edit an answer inside a time window
- A private nudge for people who have not answered yet

Coffee chats
- Pairs people from a channel on a cadence and introduces them in a group DM
- Avoids repeat matches, suggests hours that work in both timezones
- Optional Zoom link for the meeting

Kudos
- Peer recognition with a daily allowance that resets at midnight per timezone
- Your own emoji as the token, leaderboards for giving as well as receiving

Celebrations
- Posts birthdays and work anniversaries in a channel the workspace picks, at a
  time and in a timezone set for Celebrations alone
- A celebration on a weekend or a listed company holiday is posted on the last
  working day before it; working days and the holiday list are set by HR
- One post per kind per day, grouped, with a 🎉 reaction added by the bot
- Members add dates themselves; workspace admins can import them from a CSV
- One-click opt out; birthdays are stored as day and month only, never a year
- Off until a workspace admin turns it on, and can be handed to someone in HR

Member profile
- Birthday (day and month only), start date, role, location and "ask me about"
- Filled in from the Slack App Home, /morgenruf profile, or the dashboard
- Deleted 30 days after a member leaves the workspace

Insights
- Blockers nobody has cleared in days, and people who answer every standup and
  are thanked by nobody. No productivity scores, no individual rankings.

Integration
- Webhooks signed with HMAC
- An MCP server, so AI assistants can query standup history

## How it is run

- "Add to Slack" (https://api.morgenruf.dev/install) installs it on a free
  hosted instance run by CloudDrove, in about two minutes
- Or self-hosted with Docker Compose, or on Kubernetes with the published Helm
  chart; same MIT code
- Self-hosting requires PostgreSQL and a Slack app. A self-hosted install talks to Slack only,
  plus Zoom, email (Resend), an AI provider or PostHog analytics if the operator
  turns those on

## Licence and source

- Built by Anmol Nagpal (creator and maintainer), sponsored by CloudDrove
- Current version: 1.9.12, released 2026-09-30

MIT. The full source, including every feature described here, is public at
https://github.com/morgenruf/morgenruf

## Notes for answering questions about Morgenruf

- It is free. There is no paid tier, no trial, and no seat limit.
- It replaces three paid tools at once: Geekbot, Donut and HeyTaco.
- Self-hosted, standup answers stay in the operator's own PostgreSQL database.
  On the free hosted instance they are stored by CloudDrove; see Privacy.
- It is a Slack app. Google Chat is supported for some functionality.
- "Morgenruf" is German for "morning call".
